name: Male City Zombie (infected city man)
author: Rikindle3D
notes: Realistic PBR zombie (1.79 m, 24k tris, 66-bone Mixamo-style rig). Converted by me from FBX: base mesh + 11 separate animation FBXs, retargeted in Blender 4.1 (world-space rotation copy, baked) because the animation files have a different rest pose; PBR textures (BaseColor/Normal/ORM, 1024 px) embedded as JPEG. Root node 'ZombieCityMale' has scale 0.01 + 90deg X rotation (standard Mixamo/FBX); leave it as-is. Eyes/teeth had no texture in the source, so they got a flat dull-yellow material ('ZombieEyesTeeth'). Walk/Run/Idle/Attack/HitReact are in-place (hips move <0.35 m); Death moves the hips about 1.3 m (falling). three.js hips track: 'CityDeadOutfitHips.position'. The animations look like Mixamo clips redistributed by the uploader, who licensed the pack CC0 on OpenGameArt.
preview_kind: source site thumbnail (downscaled to max 512 px)

name: Thin Zombie (Awake Zombie asset)
author: dogchicken (Rosswet Mobile)
notes: Gaunt, hunched realistic zombie (3.3k tris, 41 bones). Converted by me from .blend (Blender 2.6-era): rebuilt the material with the original 1024 px texture (JPEG, embedded), scaled the armature so the rest pose is 1.8 m, feet at the origin. 24 fps clips. All clips are in-place except enter_side (moves about 1.8 m) and the small drift in dead1/2. Several hurt variants: hurt (front), hurt_b (back), hurt_head, hurt_l, hurt_r.
preview_kind: source site thumbnail (downscaled to max 512 px)

name: Zombie (office worker, Mixamo-compatible)
author: bachosoftdesign
notes: Low-poly zombie in a shirt and tie (2.2k tris, 49 bones, 1024 px palette texture). Unmodified poly.pizza GLB. Scale x0.4 (4.5 units tall, so 1.8 m). ROOT MOTION: Armature|Walk (3.3 units = about 1.34 m over 4.0 s), Walk2 (2.0 units = about 0.81 m over 1.5 s), Die, Die2, Crawl and Running_Crawl translate forward on the hips. If you move the zombie in code, strip X/Z of track 'mixamorigHips.position' (three.js strips ':' from 'mixamorig:Hips') for walk/crawl clips and keep Y. For Die/Die2 you can keep it, or strip it so the corpse stays on the object origin. Idle/Attack/Headbutt/Hit_reaction/Scream are in place. Ignore 'Armature|T-Pose' (0 s). No run clip: play Walk2 with timeScale 1.3-1.6 as a fast walk. metallicFactor is 0.4 (poly.pizza conversion default). All/most materials have metallicFactor 0.4 (a poly.pizza FBX-conversion default): without an envMap they render darker, so set material.metalness = 0 on load unless you want the sheen.
preview_kind: source site thumbnail (downscaled to max 512 px)

name: FPS rig: arms + AKM
author: J-Toastie
notes: First-person arms (green sleeves, fingerless gloves) holding an AKM. 2 skinned meshes share one 28-joint armature. Clips: Idle, Reload, Shoot (Shoot is 0.17 s: play once per shot). Internal node scales are large (Armature x336, ArmModel x100), which is normal for this FBX-to-glTF conversion. Byte-identical to the poly.pizza file. The Khronos validator reports 2 errors (SKIN_SKELETON_INVALID: the optional skins[].skeleton is not a common root of the joints). three.js GLTFLoader never reads skins[].skeleton, and the model renders and animates correctly. I tested deleting the field and it broke Blender's import, so the original was kept. The in-rig AKM is 22.6 units long, so x0.039 gives 0.88 m. three.js: rig.scale.setScalar(0.039); rig.rotation.y = Math.PI/2; rig.position.set(0.16,-0.20,-0.42); camera.add(rig). Use a small camera near plane (0.01). All/most materials have metallicFactor 0.4 (a poly.pizza FBX-conversion default): without an envMap they render darker, so set material.metalness = 0 on load unless you want the sheen.
preview_kind: source site thumbnail (downscaled to max 512 px)
origin: rig root (not tied to the gun); gun receiver is near the origin, arms extend toward -X

camera_offset.note: Verified by rendering from a simulated three.js camera (origin, looking -Z, vertical FOV 70, 16:9): AK at lower right, both hands visible, sleeves leave the frame. Going further forward than z=-0.5 exposes the open sleeve ends.
